text:
Registration opens for 2026 Michigan Cyber Summit and High School Cyber Summit
D. T. Crain
The Michigan Department of Technology, Management & Budget announced on July 8 that registration is now open for the 2026 Michigan Cyber Summit and the Michigan High School Cyber Summit. The annual events aim to provide a platform for cybersecurity education and collaboration among regional, national, and international experts.
Governor Whitmer said, “Michigan has long been a leader in cybersecurity and continues to pave the way to ensure residents remain safe online. The Michigan Cyber Summit brings the public and private sectors together to find innovative ways we can protect our state and its residents in an ever-changing digital ecosystem. The High School Cyber Summit gives our students an opportunity to explore in-demand, high-paying field careers in IT and cybersecurity. Let’s continue to work together to keep Michiganders safe.”
The fifteenth annual Michigan Cyber Summit will take place on Thursday, Oct. 15 at the Vibe Collection Showplace in Novi. The event is open to the public with sessions designed for business professionals, educators, law enforcement, and government officials. It will feature keynote speakers, panelists, and breakout sessions led by experts from across the country focusing on current strategies and technologies in cyber defense.
Tickets are available through the summit’s official website at $95 for industry attendees, $80 for government or nonprofit employees, and $50 for college students; lunch and snacks are included. Event details such as speakers and session topics will be updated as they are confirmed.
On Wednesday, Oct. 14—the day before the main summit—DTMB will host its fourth annual High School Cyber Summit at the same location in Novi. This half-day event is intended for high school students statewide who will participate in interactive activities simulating real-world cybersecurity challenges while learning about career opportunities from industry professionals.
Eric Swanson, acting chief information officer, said: “We are excited to bring back the Michigan Cyber Summit and Michigan High School Cyber Summit. These events give public and private sector professionals and students the opportunity to learn more about critical cybersecurity trends and see how we can work together to build a safer digital landscape.”
Registration for high school participants costs $35 per person including lunch; scholarships covering registration or transportation may be available on a first-come basis through application on the event website.
